questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

The lawyer said to the witness, "Tell the court what you saw on Saturday night."

options.text: The lawyer told the witness to tell the court what you saw on Saturday night.
The lawyer asked the witness to tell the court what you have seen on Saturday night.
The lawyer asked the witness to tell the court what he had seen on Saturday night.
The lawyer ordered the witness to tell the court what I had seen on Saturday night.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'The lawyer asked the witness to tell the court what he had seen on Saturday night.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is an **imperative sentence. **
 
• While changing the narration of an imperative sentence, we need to follow these steps -
 
 
• ​The **reporting verb 'said'** changes to **"asked." **
 
• The second person you will be changed into "he" 
 
• 
 The tense of the given sentence is **simple past tense (saw)** which changes to **past perfect tense (had seen)**.
 
 
• 
 "told" option is incorrect because the tense of the sentence given is incorrect.

 
 
 
 

Eventually, we will get the final sentence- The lawyer asked the witness to tell the court what he had seen on Saturday night.

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Besides, it is also an occasion to commemorate the signing of the Ramsar Convention on wetlands in 1971.

B. World Wetland Day is celebrated on 2 February to raise awareness about the critical importance of wetlands.

C. Unfortunately, these valuable wetlands are disappearing three times faster than the forest areas.

D. The Convention upholds the wetlands as the world's most economically valuable ecosystems.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'BADC'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some __grammatical or contextual __connections between them. Also, the first sentence of a passage is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. **

__
 
• **Sentence B** is the independent sentence and introduces the topic which relates to how a certain day is celebrated to raise awareness regarding the importance of wetlands. 
 
• So, sentence **B **is the first sentence after rearrangement. 
 
• **Sentence A** describes how that particular day mentioned in sentence B is also important for commemorating a certain convention. Thus, to maintain continuity, sentence **A ** comes in the **second** position. Hence, **A follows B.**__
 
• **Sentence D **which explains the importance of the convention should come **after sentence A**, to maintain continuity on the topic. 
 
• **Sentence C** is the concluding statement of the passage as it provides further information regarding how despite the critical importance of wetlands they are disappearing. 

Thus, the correct order after rearrangement is **option 1 i.e. BADC.**

***So, the correct paragraph is : (B) World Wetland Day is celebrated on 2 February to raise awareness about the critical importance of wetlands. (A) Besides, it is also an occasion to commemorate the signing of the Ramsar Convention on wetlands in 1971. (D) The Convention upholds the wetlands as the world's most economically valuable ecosystems. (C) Unfortunately, these valuable wetlands are disappearing three times faster than the forest areas.***

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

A guarantee has been given by the new government to make the long-promised reforms a reality.

options.text: The new government had given a guarantee to make the long-promised reforms a reality.
The guarantee had given a new government to make the long-promised reforms a reality.
The new government has given a guarantee to make the long-promised reforms a reality.
The new government has given the long-promised reforms a reality to make a guarantee.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'****The new government has given a guarantee to make the long-promised reforms a reality.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in **passive voice.** As per the question we have to change it into** active voice.**
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject (objective case) + has been + past participle + Object (subjective case) (Passive voice) + adjunct
 
• **Subject + has + past tense + Object (Active voice) + adjunct**
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *He has been taken out by me. (Passive voice)*
 
• *I have taken him out. (Active voice)*
 
 
 
• The **subject (objective case) **of the given sentence is ‘a guarantee’.
 
• The **object (subjective case) **of the given sentence is ‘The new government’.
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• **has been given** will be changed to **has given**.
 
• **Adjunct **is a word or phrase that constitutes an optional element or is considered of secondary importance in a sentence
 
 
• In the given sentence, *to make the long-promised reforms a reality *is the **adjunct. **
 
 

Correct sentence - The new government has given a guarantee to make the long-promised reforms a reality.

options.text: Tourists were cheated by touts so now they are careful.
Tourists is cheated by touts so now they are careful.
Tourists are cheated by touts so now they are careful.
Tourists are being cheated by touts so now they are careful.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'****Tourists are cheated by touts so now they are careful.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in **active voice.** As per the question we have to change it into** passive voice.**
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject + infinitive + Object (Active voice)
 
• **Subject (objective case) + to be + past participle + Object (subjective case) (Passive voice)**
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *The grocer sells fresh vegetables. (Active voice)*
 
• *Fresh vegetables are sold by the grocer. (Passive voice)*
 
 
 
• The **subject **of the given sentence is ‘touts’.
 
• The **object **of the given sentence is ‘tourists’.
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• **cheat **will be changed to **are cheated**.
 
• Correct sentence - **Tourists are cheated by touts so now they are careful.**

questions.question: Which of the following is true keeping in mind the character of Philip Rider?

options.text: A little learning is a dangerous thing.
A picture is worth a thousand words.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Appearances are deceptive'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given passage talks about the painter Philip Rider. He mostly painted birds and other animals. 
 
• In the passage it has been stated that - '*He was afflicted with a hunched back and a deformed, twisted hand.*' From this we can conclude that his appearance was not pleasing. 
 
• Despite his appearance, according to the passage, he had a tender heart and he loved all creatures. 
 
• The passage goes on to tell a story of how Rider saved the life of a bird which had been shot. 
 
• Thus, despite his terrible appearance, he was a kind-hearted person. 
 
• So, **option 2** or **appearances can be deceptive** is true keeping in mind the character of Philip Rider. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A little learning is a dangerous thing - **A small amount of knowledge can mislead individuals into believing that they are more experienced and expert than what is actually the case.
 
• **A picture is worth a thousand words **- complex and sometimes multiple ideas can be conveyed by a single still image, which conveys its meaning or essence more effectively than a mere verbal description.
 
• **Actions speak louder than words - **what someone actually does means more than what they say they will do.
